title: Computational foundations: factorization, KL, and optimization

items.title: Latent-variable joint and observed-data factorization
items.statement: On measurable parameter, observation, and latent spaces with sigma-finite observation and latent reference measures, take one specified jointly measurable nonnegative complete-data density normalized on every parameter fibre. Its observed marginal is the latent integral, and a normalized latent-fibre density is defined only when that marginal is positive and finite. This supplied joint function is not inferred from separate likelihood versions and requires no choice axiom.

references.title: Mario A. T. Figueiredo, Lecture Notes on the EM Algorithm (2004)

items.title: Kullback–Leibler divergence is nonnegative
items.statement: Under AC and the published directional KL convention, D(P||Q) is nonnegative and equals zero exactly when P=Q. For finite-valued nonnegative measurable gamma and probability density q on a measure space, if 0<Z=integral gamma<infinity, q is supported by gamma, and integral q(|log gamma|+|log q|) is finite, then log Z=integral q(log gamma-log q)+D(q mu||(gamma/Z)mu). The density ratio and absolute-continuity hypotheses are proved locally.

references.title: Mario A. T. Figueiredo, Lecture Notes on the EM Algorithm (2004)
references.locator: §2, equations (7)–(9), PDF pp. 3–5; the source's parameter-equality clause is excluded

items.title: Gradient descent
items.statement: For a continuously differentiable real objective on an open Euclidean domain, update in the negative gradient direction using either a supplied fixed positive step or Armijo backtracking; stop at a zero gradient or the caller's stopping rule.

references.title: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization

items.title: Damped Newton method
items.statement: For a twice continuously differentiable real objective, solve the Newton system with a symmetric positive-definite Hessian by Cholesky factorization and use Armijo backtracking with a Newton-decrement stopping rule. Halt if the gradient is zero or a required positive-definite solve is unavailable.

references.title: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization

items.title: The observed density is the latent marginal under Tonelli
items.statement: For a jointly measurable normalized complete-data density on sigma-finite reference spaces, the latent marginal is measurable and normalized. It is finite almost everywhere; positive finite fibres define measurable normalized latent densities. A product-measurable complex-valued h may be exchanged by Fubini when its absolute hp integral is finite.

references.title: Mario A. T. Figueiredo, Lecture Notes on the EM Algorithm (2004)
references.locator: §1, equation (1), PDF pp. 1–2; the Tonelli and Fubini arguments are supplied locally

items.title: Armijo backtracking terminates for strict descent directions
items.statement: For either authored backtracking procedure, if the objective is differentiable on an open domain and the current direction has strictly negative directional derivative, geometric Armijo backtracking accepts a positive step after finitely many reductions.

references.title: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization
references.locator: Chapter 9 §9.2 backtracking line search and §9.5 Algorithm 9.5, PDF pp. 477–483 and 498–505

items.title: Gradient descent rate under strong convexity and smoothness
items.statement: If f has an attained minimum, its gradient is L-Lipschitz, it is mu-strongly convex with 0<mu<=L, and gradient descent uses step 1/L, then f(x_k)-f* <= (1-mu/L)^k (f(x_0)-f*).

references.title: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization
references.locator: Chapter 9 §9.3.1, PDF pp. 477–483; the stated fixed-step form is proved locally

items.title: Newton's method has local quadratic convergence under a Lipschitz Hessian
items.statement: Let f be C2 near an interior critical point x* with positive-definite Hessian and locally Lipschitz Hessian. From a sufficiently close start, damped Newton with Armijo backtracking accepts unit steps and satisfies ||x_(k+1)-x*|| <= C ||x_k-x*||^2 for a finite constant C. This is local and makes no global optimality claim.

references.title: Stephen Boyd and Lieven Vandenberghe, Convex Optimization
references.locator: Chapter 9 §9.5.3, PDF pp. 498–505; the local theorem is proved under the BCS-20 hypotheses

title: Computational foundations: factorization, KL, and optimization — Examples

items.title: Equal-variance Gaussian location KL
items.statement: For P=N(a,tau^2) and Q=N(b,tau^2), with tau>0, the KL divergence is (a-b)^2/(2 tau^2), hence nonnegative.

items.title: A multimodal nonconvex objective
items.statement: The smooth objective f(x)=(x^2-1)^2 has two distinct global minima and a local maximum between them; no global convergence guarantee is inferred for either local algorithm.

items.title: A finite mixture latent factorization
items.statement: For finitely many normalized component densities and positive weights summing to one, the complete-data density p(x,j)=w_j f_j(x) has observed marginal sum_j w_j f_j(x), and its normalized positive finite fibers give the component-label conditional density.

items.title: A zero-normalizer latent fiber
items.statement: A normalized complete-data density may have an observed fiber with marginal zero; on that fiber the ratio p(x,z)/m(x) is undefined and supplies no pointwise conditional density.

items.title: Gradient descent on a strongly convex quadratic
items.statement: For f(x)=1/2||x-b||^2, the gradient and Hessian are x-b and I. With mu=1 and a valid smoothness constant L=2, step 1/L gives objective gap 4^-k times the initial gap, so the claimed (1/2)^k bound holds.
